channel.title: Comments for page "Dr. Gray's Proposal"
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Dr. Gray's Proposal"

item.title: Holy shit.
item.content:encoded:
This article is beautiful. If I were pressed to take a concept used by eldritch gods and use it to make a story to bring tears to your eyes, I'd stumble and fall.

Granted a few grammatical errors in the article (for example, the pronouns when talking about SCP-001-FR herself alternate between 'his' and 'hers' often), its swiftly become one of my favorite articles on the site. And even giving it multiple rereads hit home on the sentiments delivered by 05-13 and Agent Klein.

This needs to be on the list with all of the other English proposals, it deserves to be read and pondered

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
001 proposals do tend to drive a lot of engagement, but that's mostly due to the author(s) advertising them in chat, over Discord, etc., and because the SCP-001 hub page is well-trafficked.

As a translated work, the author was not around to advertise this directly, and it's not linked on the hub page with the English proposals. As such, I imagine that the majority of engagement with this 001 proposal happened when it was initially created and displayed on the Recently Created Pages module. Translated articles also generally don't perform as well as English articles, for a variety of reasons.

I'm sorry to flirt with necroposting, but since no one has responded and I spent a few minutes puzzling over the language I thought I should respond.

I'd say it's much better to replace organism with body. I'm not quite sure of the exact grammatical terms here, but as a native English speaker the phrase "[she] has an organism" implies to me that the object is an entity separate from her, whereas "[she] has a body" reads as a description of her physical nature.

item.title: Ein Sof
item.content:encoded:
I'm sorry, but the language for this Class is just WAY to advanced for me. Could someone offer a layman's description of it for me?
Thanks!

Edit: I had to sit down for a good while, but what I read it as is this:
So we had to add a bit more so that this thing that doesn't physically exist behaves predictably, and so that some other thing that controls the universe doesn't get too angry.
Tell me if I'm wrong.

item.title: Re: Hardest novote ever, I think.
item.content:encoded: I can guarantee you that us French members follow very closely every critic addressed to our work, especially when it's such a recent one, moreover one which matches with our current criteria as a whole writing community. We hear your point and thank you for your time and evaluation, as well as all the other members who took the time to read, vote and share their thoughts about the article!

item.title: Hardest novote ever, I think.
item.content:encoded:
I'll be short, but concise1:

+ show block
– hide block

What I dislike:
- Exposition. Tons of exposition, which should not be that much of a problem in measured quantities. At many points the article explained itself way too much, took our hands too far, etc.
- The characters were incredibly naive in many aspects. Given the core nature of the Foundation2, people would most likely suspect of other motives. The mirage argument is plausible and could had been a pretty interesting approach to address further. Even though I understand what the author was aiming for I can't fully support a situaqtion in which people take the anomaly's word for granted, unless that's part of her anomaly, which would give the article a grimmier/fridger undertone to it.

What I liked and disliked at the same time:
- The pomposity. Hell, the characters are self-aware of it, but there's something that I find somewhat appealing to it.

What I liked:
- The characters, albeit not as believeable as I would have wanted them to be, were definitely quite sympathetic. Moreover, I actually take my word back because I loved the interaction between Jhon and Tristan. In that moment, I was able to care for them and their fate. That si remarkable.
- This story is emotional-driven. I realized that it was trying to pull my heartstrings from the beggining and never dropped them. By the time I finished I had felt quite emotionally invested, despite every flaw I spotted during the read.

In conclusion, the site is huge. Over 4k articles, from which I probably read a good 70% by now, since I've been struggling with keeping up with the last 2 series. Anyways, after a while, you develope an instinct to feel whether an article has that X factor that makes it stand above the rest or not. Said X factor is not necessarily a surefire because I give equal credit to a solid execution, and flopping the former is way more forgiving since people will still like a neatly-packed article. My impression is that this one excelled at that, making it stand and forcing me to care; however, when thinking on its technical details, it falls short for me.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

Thus: novote. I'm not sure these mistakes can be as easily addressed since it was originally in French. Still, I enjoyed this article more than many articles I have upvoted for in the past.

Footnotes
1. which means I am deliberately not mentions each and every single thing that I liked/disliked but rather what my brain allow me to articulate so late in the night.
2. even though this doesn't need to be the case

item.content:encoded:
This is incredible. It's one of the best pieces of fiction my eyes have gazed upon in my years of scraping paper and code for reading material.

It breaks away from 001 clichés so well, and even when the plot turns to be another rendition of the world being a dream, it does it beautifully, in a heartwarming fashion I have never experienced before.

Well deserved +1, although I wish I could give this piece the true honors it deserves.
